issues.legal_issue: The supervisory jurisdiction of a High Court cannot be used to correct an inferior court’s ordinary error when the court acted within its authority and the complaint does not disclose a jurisdictional or procedural failure.
material_facts: The petitioner challenged orders made in execution proceedings by petitioning the High Court under Article 227 of the Constitution.

An appeal was available against an order under Order XXI, Rule 92, and the dispute also raised a question under Section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure for which an appeal was available under the law then in force; even if no appeal lay, a revision under Section 115 was available.

The subordinate court had not failed to exercise jurisdiction, disregarded natural justice, or adopted a procedure contrary to law; the petitioner’s complaint did not establish an error of law or an error apparent on the face of the record.
issues.conclusion: The petition under Article 227 was misconceived, and the High Court had no jurisdiction to interfere with the subordinate court’s orders on the grounds advanced.
issues.legal_principle: Article 227 gives the High Court limited supervisory jurisdiction to ensure that an inferior court or tribunal functions within the limits of its authority; it does not make the High Court an appellate tribunal for reviewing evidence or correcting ordinary errors of fact or law. A mere wrong decision is insufficient. The Court also noted the available appeal under Order XLIII, Rule 1(j), the appealability under Sections 47 and 2(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure as they then stood, and the alternative remedy of revision under Section 115.

predicates.supervisory_petition_against_lower_court: A party asks a higher court to use supervisory jurisdiction to interfere with an order of a lower court.
predicates.lower_court_acted_within_authority: The lower court acted within the authority given to it.
predicates.no_jurisdictional_or_procedural_failure: The lower court did not fail to exercise jurisdiction, violate natural justice, or use a procedure contrary to law.

issues.definition: When a supervisory petition challenges an order made within the lower court’s authority and no jurisdictional or procedural failure is shown, supervisory interference is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: An adjustment between a decree-holder and a judgment-debtor cannot be certified to displace an execution sale once the sale has intervened in the rights of an auction-purchaser.
material_facts: Property was sold in execution of a decree, and an auction-purchaser acquired an interest in it.
After the sale, an application sought to have the decree recorded as satisfied on the basis of an alleged payment by the surety before the sale.
The surety had not applied under Order XXI, Rule 2 to have the alleged adjustment certified, and the required deposit to set aside the sale under Order XXI, Rule 89 had not been made.
issues.conclusion: Once the execution sale has intervened in the rights of a third-party purchaser, the alleged adjustment cannot be certified to nullify the sale; the sale may be set aside only through the applicable procedure for doing so.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order XXI, Rules 2 and 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an adjustment cannot be certified to defeat rights that have intervened through an execution sale, and the sale is to be confirmed if no application to set it aside is made under Rule 89. The Court relied on Nanhelal & Anr. v. Umrao Singh, which held that the purchaser’s intervening interest cannot be disregarded and identified the Rule 89 procedure as the means for the judgment-debtor to get rid of a duly carried-out sale.

rule.if: execution_sale_proceeding and auction_sale_completed and purchaser_interest_intervened and adjustment_certification_sought_after_sale

predicates.execution_sale_proceeding: The proceeding concerns enforcement of a decree through a sale of property.
predicates.auction_sale_completed: The property has been sold at an execution auction.
predicates.purchaser_interest_intervened: A purchaser has acquired an interest through the execution sale.
predicates.adjustment_certification_sought_after_sa: A party seeks to have an adjustment between the decree-holder and judgment-debtor certified after the auction sale.

issues.definition: If an adjustment is sought to be certified after a completed execution auction has given a purchaser an intervening interest, the adjustment cannot displace the sale.
